checks.label: When we multiply a function by a positive constant its graph is stretched or compressed vertically: 2x² keeps every input and doubles every output, so the heights 4, 1, 1 and 4 become 8, 2, 2 and 8 in the arrows, labels and table; ½x² takes (2, 4) to (2, 2); at every top-handle setting each height arrow is that many times its start

Multiplying all outputs by −1 gives a reflection about the x-axis: −x² keeps every input and gives the heights −4, −1, −1 and −4, so (2, 4) goes to (2, −4), and the right answer for −√x takes (9, 3) straight down to (9, −3)

−(2x)² is a vertical reflection across the x-axis and a horizontal compression by a factor of 2: each input is halved and each height changes sign, so (2, 4) goes to (1, −4), as the right answer on the inside-and-out screen draws

Each real-world value converts to its 4 to 20 mA signal with the linear equation y = mx + b: S(p) = 0.16p + 4 is p ÷ 100 stretched by 16 and lifted 4 mA, so 0% sends 4 mA and 100% sends 20 mA, and at 50% the picture reads 0.5, then 8 mA, then 12 mA as the stretch and the lift arrive

Multiplying the input squeezes the graph sideways: √(2x) gives 1, 2 and 3 at 0.5, 2 and 4.5, as the arrows, labels and table show; √(3x) gives 3 at x = 3; √(−x) gives 2 at x = −4, takes only inputs of 0 and below, and its table reads −1, −4 and −9

Every worked number is right: −x² + 2 gives −2 at x = 2 and −(x² + 2) gives −6; lifting first would send 16 × 4.5 = 72 mA; a gain of 8 sends 8 × 0.5 + 4 = 8 mA at 50%, halving the whole signal gives 6 mA and the stretch alone 4 mA; 3√(2x) takes (2, 2) to (2, 6) and (9, 3) to (4.5, 9); the wave with a peak of 2 lifted 1 runs from −1 to 3, as its labels read
Before Check a puzzle draws no answer; the right answer moves the graph there with its labels and draws nothing in red; each wrong answer draws its own slip in red and leaves the graph where it was

The picture tells the truth: every dot sits on its own graph inside the grid, every arrow runs from an axis to its own dot, the dashed copy stays where the graph started, and a pull lands only on the screen's settings with the rule above rewritten to match
Every demonstration has settled within 4.5 s, starting after the 0.35 s screen fade; every answer, right or wrong, has arrived within 2.5 s of Check
